name: Canopy Growth Corporation
headline_status: Canopy Growth is a Canadian cannabis producer and Storz & Bickel vaporizer maker that is growing again in 2026 on medical and international sales, but still reports losses.
summary: Canopy Growth is one of Canada's best-known cannabis producers. It sells adult-use brands such as Tweed, 7ACRES, DOJA and, since its March 2026 purchase of MTL Cannabis, MTL; runs Canada's largest medical cannabis service through Spectrum Therapeutics and related clinics; and owns German vaporizer maker Storz & Bickel. It also holds a non-controlling, unconsolidated interest in Canopy USA, which owns Acreage, Wana and Jetty and a stake in TerrAscend, giving it indirect U.S. exposure without consolidating U.S. THC operations. In the quarter ended September 30, 2026 (fiscal Q2 2027), net revenue rose 22% to C$81.4 million, driven by a 141% jump in international cannabis sales, mostly to Germany and Poland, and gains in Canadian medical and adult-use. It recorded a C$40.7 million net loss, largely from fair-value charges on Canopy USA assets, and a small adjusted EBITDA loss of C$2.9 million. Management under CEO Luc Mongeau says it is close to positive adjusted EBITDA and is building an EU-GMP supply chain, including new U.K. and Australian product launches.

faq.q: Does Canopy Growth own U.S. cannabis businesses?
faq.a: Not directly in its financial statements. It holds a non-controlling, unconsolidated interest in Canopy USA, which owns Acreage, Wana and Jetty and holds TerrAscend shares. Canopy recorded C$35.8 million of fair-value charges on those assets in its September 2026 quarter.

No. It reported a C$40.7 million net loss and a C$2.9 million adjusted EBITDA loss for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, though management says positive adjusted EBITDA is within reach during fiscal 2027.
